rows.notes: Aggregate counts only. No raw click target text or field values are retained.

rows.statement: Prefer tracker summaries that prioritize status changes, next actions, follow-ups, risks, and information retrieval over generic activity lists.
rows.evidenceSummary: An explicit multi-part feedback review repeatedly identified status reports, next actions, follow-up decisions, risk detection, and finding scattered information as the most valuable outcomes.

rows.statement: Keep team-facing planning views high level and limited to meaningful deliverables and activities in the next two to three weeks, with detailed intelligence available underneath.
rows.evidenceSummary: Explicit feedback requested a concise three-week team view and specifically rejected showing every open project when it lacks a meaningful near-term deliverable or activity.

rows.statement: Prefer current operational status derived by reconciling available sources, while clearly flagging source-of-truth mismatches for correction.
rows.evidenceSummary: Explicit feedback described stale and incomplete project reporting, asked for a live refresh before reports, and stated that newer operational evidence should be used while outdated system records are separately flagged.

rows.statement: Distinguish confirmed dates, system-scheduled dates, and tracker-calculated dates; when no target exists, calculate a best estimate and request validation.
rows.evidenceSummary: Explicit feedback requested visible date provenance and confirmed that missing target dates should be calculated from the best available information but marked for validation.

rows.statement: Prefer attention views that suppress already acknowledged or actively tracked work and emphasize new, changed, stalled, missing, or at-risk items.
rows.evidenceSummary: Explicit feedback called already-tracked items noisy and asked for delta reporting, stalled-item alerts, missing-step detection, and a way to acknowledge known work.

rows.statement: Treat the dashboard as the primary orientation and decision workspace while monitoring whether deeper planning and ticket views gain sustained use.
rows.evidenceSummary: Across six summarized sessions, 58 of 74 recorded interactions occurred in the dashboard context, compared with 10 in project views and 6 in role views; no durable usage signal yet exists for the other top-level views.

rows.statement: Prompt follow-up on customer-waiting work after about two days by default, with earlier escalation when delay threatens a critical commitment.
rows.evidenceSummary: Explicit feedback gave a two-day default for customer follow-up and asked that critical dependencies shorten the threshold.

rows.title: Establish trusted status reconciliation
rows.observedProblem: The tracker cannot currently show whether project status is fresh, complete, or consistent across sources, so users may need to double-check reports before acting.
rows.evidenceSummary: Explicit feedback reported a stale status, incomplete workload coverage, and conflicting reliability across operational sources. The current project-item model stores a source label but has no freshness timestamp, verification state, conflict indicator, coverage check, or date provenance.
rows.expectedImpact: Fewer incorrect statuses, dates, and owners; less duplicate verification; greater confidence in daily and team-facing reports.
rows.validationPlan: Pilot provenance and mismatch handling on a limited project set. Track incorrect statuses, wrong dates or owners, unresolved source conflicts, manual verification time, and user trust before expanding or adding integrations.
rows.reversibility: Use additive fields and a gated reconciliation view so the workflow can be disabled without removing existing project or item data.

rows.title: Add delta and exception-focused operational views
rows.observedProblem: Current dashboard and planning views summarize present state but do not explain what changed, verify workload coverage, suppress acknowledged items, or audit what was omitted from a report.
rows.evidenceSummary: Explicit feedback prioritized a daily roll-up, a concise three-week team view, and a missed-item audit, while describing already-tracked work as noise. Aggregate telemetry also shows the dashboard is the dominant interaction context, making it the most relevant place to test an exception-first summary.
rows.expectedImpact: Less rereading and manual searching, earlier detection of missed or stalled work, and more focused team discussions.
rows.validationPlan: Prototype read-only delta, coverage, acknowledgement, and omission-audit views. Compare missed items, false alerts, time spent reviewing, repeated manual searches, and follow-up timeliness against the current workflow.
rows.reversibility: Introduce the outputs as optional views without replacing the existing dashboard, Daily Plan, or project boards.

rows.title: Evaluate project document lookup
rows.observedProblem: Project work may require substantial manual searching for drawings and other files because the tracker does not expose authorized document locations or retrieval paths.
rows.evidenceSummary: Explicit feedback identified finding project drawings as a recurring time cost and suggested linked cloud access. The current interface and data model contain no document lookup or project-to-document reference.
rows.expectedImpact: Faster information retrieval and fewer missed project artifacts, provided access controls and source boundaries remain intact.
rows.validationPlan: Start with a read-only proof of concept for a small set of non-sensitive project document references. Measure successful finds, search time, false matches, permission failures, and whether users still need to search manually.
rows.reversibility: Keep lookup read-only and feature-gated, with no document copying or permission changes; disable the view if results are not reliable.
